exposure: optimal antenatal corticosteroid (ACS) administration timing (>=24 h to <=7 days)
suboptimal antenatal corticosteroid (ACS) administration timing (>7 days)
maternal-obstetrical factors (nulliparity, preterm premature rupture of membranes, chronic hypertension, asymptomatic cervical shortening)
cohort: The study included 399 women who prematurely delivered a viable neonate between 24+0 and 36+6 gestational weeks, following antenatal corticosteroid treatment.
finding: Optimal antenatal corticosteroid timing was associated with nulliparity and preterm premature rupture of membranes, whereas suboptimal timing was linked to chronic hypertension and asymptomatic cervical shortening, with optimal timing also associated with higher neonatal intensive care unit admission.
birth_weight: Measured and used as an adjustment variable.
